best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Changli's signature weapon that's not only fantastic for her but also usable on all damage-focused Sword users who have a large portion of their damage originating from Resonance Skill damage. Offers a huge main stat of CRIT DMG% granting excellent scaling, 12% permanent ATK% and up to 56% increased Resonance Skill DMG% which should be at or close to full power during the bulk of your rotation when opening with one or two resonance skills.

cons: Basic Attack damage dealers are few and far between, and aside from a select few most of them are really outdated and powercrept, so her synergies are either too old to perform or too account-dependent;
Personal damage is among the lowest of all Hybrid/buffer-type characters;
S5 is a big rotation time decrease, S6 provides added team buffs. A good amount of her value is locked behind her last 2 Sequence nodes.
pros: The premier and only F2P Basic Attack buffer in the game. Fantastic with all Basic Attack damage dealers;
Has one of the fastest rotations in the game and is optimization/quickswap-friendly;
Requires next to no investment to perform in terms of build quality and weapon choice;

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Sanhua is a 5-star Glacio Sword Hybrid buffer character specialized towards buffing Basic Attack damage dealers. She rotates in and out of the field remarkably quicker than most her peers, gives them a sufficient amount of buffs and lets the DPS she's paired with take the spotlight.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Sanhua's primary rotation goal is to create and detonate Ice Creations to generate her Concerto as quickly as possible. She generates the following Ice Creations through the following attacks:
Each restores 15 Concerto and deals some amount of damage (we listed them in the order of lowest to highest damage above).

Sanhua detonates these Ice Creations through her Forte Heavy Attack, called Detonate. It can be activated any time, however it requires you to charge it up and time it with her Forte. A little arrow icon will appear when you hold down Basic Attack on Sanhua and you can release it to make it stop. A regular Heavy Attack is performed if instantly released or released in the grey area. If released in the blue area though, Sanhua performs Heavy: Detonate. Timing the release of the Basic Attack button correctly and quickly is essential to properly performing Sanhua rotations. This timing window is made bigger when Sanhua generates any Ice Creation, allowing for faster, more lenient timings.

Once the animation is complete, Heavy: Detonate will shatter all Ice Creations and generate a large amount of Concerto Energy. Paired with her Intro, Skill and Ultimate, at S5 (which has the hidden property of dealing Glacier damage twice, giving 15 extra Concerto), it gives Sanhua enough Concerto to get off her Outro. A second Heavy: Detonate will be needed at S4 and below, which will be more difficult to time than the first.

Other important aspects of Sanhua's kit are her Outro, which gives 38% Basic Attack DMG Amplification for 14s to the next character, expiring upon swap. This is what gives Sanhua her team synergies. Her S6 also provides 20% team-wide ATK.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Sanhua has been a staple F2P meta character since her release. Her and Mortefi are specialized towards amplifying a specific damage type by 38%, which is a pretty large amount for how dated the characters are, all things considered. Paired with the Moonlit Clouds Echo set and their S6, they're able to provide a good amount of buffs to any character of their corresponding damage types.

Recently, Sanhua has seen a resurgence in usability, because two key Basic Attack damage dealers have released: Luuk Herssen, and most importantly, Suoming.  Suoming has everything Sanhua wants to shine as a buffer: that is, just dealing a lot of Basic Attack damage. Nothing else. Raw Basic Attack damage numbers are exactly what Sanhua buffs, and while Luuk is also a viable choice to use as Sanhua's Main DPS, he specializes in Tune Strain which Sanhua has no synergy with whatsoever, making her significantly outclassed by Denia and Lynae who have affinities with the archetype.

In terms of other team options though? Before Luuk, the Basic Attack damage archetype had not seen a non-overly specialized DPS (such as Cartethyia) come out since Camellya. Indeed, a lot of Sanhua's best teams are still confined to the long-since outdated 1.x version's meta, like Encore and Havoc Rover for example. She in fact finds better use cases in teams with modern DPS characters who have no better fully F2P teammate alternatives. Teams like Hiyuki Sanhua Verina have come to exist, simply because Sanhua gives small amounts of buffs and allows the DPS to take as much of the spotlight on-field as possible thanks to her lightning fast rotation. It gives her a tiny bit more staying power long-term, but her best use cases are still in Basic Attack damage teams by far.

In conclusion, Sanhua is a great choice for F2P Basic Attack buffing. Sanhua is never truly best in slot in any current team, however she's a very close second for a lot of Basic Attack DPS. She can allow players to skip pulling premium Supports for Basic Attack DPS characters while still performing well enough to clear endgame content with a proper build. This makes her a staple investment for many accounts looking to round out their endgame teams.

synergies.commentary: Sanhua's premium synergies. These limited Basic Attack Main DPS characters make great use of her buffs, Suoming being ideal thanks to her general scaling while Luuk is more reliant on Tune Strain. Camellya is a really old choice that can clear some low-difficulty endgames with enough effort.

Sanhua's F2P synergies include the old reliable Encore, the best permanent banner DPS, and Havoc Rover if you really want to make use of DPS Rover. Neither of them fully rely on Basic Attack DMG but mostly do, so Sanhua works decently here, although these are really old F2P pairings so don't expect them to shatter your expectations in endgame.

Sanhua's teams generally go alongside DPS characters that don't scale off any specialized mechanics, so Shorekeeper and Verina are the best generalist Support options most of the time. Luuk does scale off of Tune Strain though, which Mornye can help with if you want to use that team in specific.
